Hi Chris / Priya,

Thanks again for the time today - great conversation and appreciate you walking through Acme's evaluation criteria. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we're aligned before the technical kickoff.

Key pain points you shared:
- Latency spikes on peak queries (current p95 ~600ms) impacting customer-facing flows
- High per-token inference spend for interactive experiences (goal: ~30% cost reduction)
- Model output consistency across diverse prompt templates; need reproducible quality
- Data residency & key management requirements for regulated customers (KMS + audit logs)

Goals for the bakeoff:
1) Demonstrate consistent latency improvements (target p95 <200ms, p50 <100ms)
2) Evaluate quality across 3 core use-cases (support summarization, recommendations, and chat assistant)
3) Measure unit economics: cost per 1M tokens at target latency SLAs
4) Verify security controls (VPC/private deployment + KMS integrations)

What we'll provide (attached):
- acme-bakeoff-matrix.xlsx (test matrix + success criteria)
- redwood-demo-recording.mp4 (short walkthrough of our Dedicated setup)

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Confirm test owners and dataset scope (please reply with who will own each test)
- Schedule 60-min technical kickoff (we propose Wed 9/3 or Thu 9/4)
- Redwood to share test harness and SOW draft for timeline/SLAs

If you're aligned, we'll kick off the technical run next week and loop in Jordan for the test setup.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole

Hey Marissa - thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side before we lock dates: 

1) For the quality evaluation, can you confirm whether you expect to run both automatic metrics and a small blind human evaluation? We'll assign reviewers either way but want to align on sample sizes.
2) Can VendorX be included as the third arm? We want a head-to-head across our shortlist (VendorX, Redwood, and Open model baseline).
3) Dataset: most of our prompts are short (avg 18 tokens) but we have a minority of long-form summarization prompts (~2-3k tokens). Can the test harness support both?
4) Timeline: we prefer the runs to complete in a 5 business day window to avoid drift. Is that feasible?

Alex Zhou from our team will own the test logistics - looping him in once we confirm dates.

Also, can you share the SOW draft and the test scripts up front so our security/compliance folks can review?

Thanks,

Hi Chris / Priya - Jordan from Redwood's Solutions Eng team here. Thanks for the detailed follow-up. Below is a concise plan for the bakeoff and how we'll measure success so your engineers/security folks have what they need to review.

Proposed bakeoff design (high-level):
- Arms: Redwood Dedicated (pinned model versions), VendorX (their managed endpoint), Open Baseline (open-source model hosted in the same infra)
- Workloads: 3 buckets - chat assistant (interactive), summarization (long-form), and recommendation/rerank (short prompt, high throughput)
- Test harness: we will run each arm on the same prompt corpus, with fixed sampling seeds and identical decoding params to keep variability low
- Metrics to capture: p50/p95 latency, 95th tail latency under synthetic burst, throughput (tokens/s), cost per 1M tokens (USD), and quality (blind human evaluation + automated checks for hallucination rate and token overlap)
- Security checks: private VPC test, KMS key usage verification, and audit log snapshot for each run

Sample sizes & timing:
- Automatic runs: ~5k prompts per arm across buckets (should complete in 48-72 hours with parallel slots)
- Human eval: 300 sampled outputs per arm (3 raters each, rubric provided) - we can accelerate if Acme increases reviewer headcount

Artifacts we'll share immediately:
- redwood-bakeoff-test-scripts.zip (test harness + instructions)
- sow-draft-acme.docx (timeline, SLAs, and estimated cost)
- Link to dataset and rubric: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C4D

Questions for Acme:
1) Confirm inclusion of VendorX as an arm (Chris suggested yes)
2) Agree on human eval rubric and whether Acme will provide raters or Redwood should recruit independent raters
3) Confirm target completion window (5 business days) and approved kickoff slot - we suggested Wed 9/3 or Thu 9/4; Jordan is available both days.

If that looks good, Marissa and I will finalize the SOW and lock a kickoff.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
